children: Zcash miner Fortitude has secured shareholder approval in its merger-driven push to list on Nasdaq. If it clears the exchange's final review, the company plans to trade under the ticker TUDE.

The Block reported on Nov. 20 that shareholders of healthcare company HeartSciences approved the merger with Fortitude with about 86% support. After the merger, the company will be renamed Fortitude Mining Group. Nasdaq's final approval is still pending, and a trading start date has not been set.
Chief Executive Officer Jamie Leverton said the shareholder vote opens the way for Fortitude to become a leading publicly traded Zcash mining platform.

Fortitude was spun out of Foundry's mining division in January last year. Foundry is a subsidiary of Digital Currency Group. The company operates 60 megawatts of power infrastructure across seven sites in the U.S. Its Zcash mining hashrate rose about 15% to 5.4 GSol/s from 4.7 GSol/s in early October.

The company is also expanding its equipment base. Last month, it signed a deal with Bitmain for priority access to next-generation Zcash mining machines. The agreement includes an intent to purchase up to $100 million of equipment. Earlier, in July, Fortitude signed a $31.5 million agreement to buy 9,000 Z15 Pro mining rigs.

Zcash traded at about $753 as of Nov. 20. That was roughly 55% below the $1,680 recorded about two months earlier, but the token has still posted one of the strongest year-to-date gains among the top 20 cryptocurrencies, alongside Hyperliquid (HYPE).

title: Zcash Miner Fortitude Wins Shareholder Approval for Merger, Clears Nasdaq Listing Hurdle
